Sideloading source for Feather, AltStore and SideStore, updated with each release

.github/source/make_source.py turns the published releases into an AltStore
source (apps.json) with every IPA, newest first. The new "source" job runs it
after publish and stores apps.json on the "source" branch, whose raw address
the README gives.

HUD: phone battery and a clock in the top left, switchable in OPTIONS

- OPTIONS > DISPLAY: BATTERY (on/off, listed only where a battery can be
  read: the iPhone build) and CLOCK (off / real time / game time), saved in
  game.ini like the other options. On touch, a tap on the clock switches
  real time and game time.
- The HUD sits right of the minimap (or at the safe-area corner without it)
  and hides with it under menus, battles and top panels. Game time is the
  CLOCK structure's (world.clock_minutes()), drawn in gold. Texts change at
  most once a second (game time) or every 10 s / at the minute.
- iOS: a small Godot iOS plugin (project/ios/plugins/pokewilds_battery)
  keeps UIDevice's battery in POKEWILDS_BATTERY, read with
  OS.get_environment; no Godot headers. Its library is built before the
  export in the ios job (xcrun) and in tools/ios_xtool (Swift's clang),
  where Package.swift links it. Desktop and server read nothing and show
  no battery.
- server/status_hud_test.gd: the HUD, options, game.ini and the clock tap
  in a real game (headless, throwaway data folder).

CI: faster builds (Mac job alongside the smoke test, LTO and import caches)

- ios no longer waits for smoke; publish needs smoke instead, so only a
  pack that passed the smoke test is still released.
- The engine is LTO bitcode recompiled at every link: Apple's ld and xtool's
  lld keep their LTO cache between runs (keyed on the engine profile and the
  linker).
- Godot's import cache (.godot) is restored in smoke, ios, ios_xtool and
  server: only changed assets are imported again.
- ios_xtool: no disk cleanup (the runner has ~80 GB free).
- The server smoke test prints as it goes, to see where its 5 minutes go.
xtool: do not fail at the end where there is no wslpath [skip ci]

Versions: commit count in CI and in the local xtool build, so both builds of a commit match

CI numbered versions by run, which a local build cannot know. Both now use
MAJOR.MINOR from the iOS preset plus the commit count of main (also the
CFBundleVersion), so an IPA built with tools/ios_xtool from the same commit
has the same version and build id as the CI one and plays with the CI server.
Merge stream-spikes: tile streams never over ~4 ms in a frame, setup sliced, teleports prepared
Merge sheet-no-readback: drop the Gen 3 branch in TexturePixels

CI: the IPA's visible version goes up with every build (0.10.<build>)

The iOS preset's short_version gives MAJOR.MINOR (now 0.10) and the build
number fills the third part; CFBundleVersion stays 100 + build number. The
release title and notes show the version.

CI: one release per commit with the IPA and the server, published only when both pass

A single workflow creates a draft release, the iOS and server jobs upload
their files, and the release is published as Latest only when both passed;
a failed or cancelled build deletes the draft. The README links use
releases/latest/download, so they always give a matching pair.
